issues.title: Redesign the launcher UI
issues.pin: This panel is the target, and the premise this pin carried is now stale: it said the controls are one flat column with no grouping and no first step. Both shipped. The rows are grouped into tabs (#26, proved: TABS at settings.mjs:43, one pane per tab) and the first step is the lobby, where Load opens the state menu (#33). What is left is the parity list the board measures: 10 of the 29 spec rows are unbuilt and the Input tab has no row to show, which is engine work under #32, #17 and #28 rather than a redesign. This pin stays open as the umbrella for the panel as a whole; it is not blocked on a design decision.

issues.title: Shared lobby URL with port claiming
issues.pin: The room code is the lobby, top right, and clicking it copies the link. Two players pair for real, and a phone-shaped browser is one of them: measured over the routable tailnet address, both claim a port and the touch overlay draws. Two defects had to go first, and both hid behind loopback. signal.mjs sent claims as an object while lobby.mjs calls .indexOf on it, so every state event threw and no claim ever rendered (9fee67ca). Then crypto.randomUUID, which exists only in a secure context: http://127.0.0.1 is one by exemption and a tailnet IP is not, so the page could mint neither a room nor an identity on the only origin a visitor uses (f303d4a8). A third defect was in the offer itself: gathered() cut ICE gathering off after 3 seconds without checking that a srflx candidate had arrived, so on a slow network the offer went out with LAN addresses only. Measured here the first srflx lands at 11 ms while gathering is still open after 12 s, so the cutoff is now a ceiling and the srflx arrival releases the offer (c51bf783). Also measured over an https origin, which is what a shared link really has and which plain http on an IP is not: both ports claim and the data channel opens there too. On the two-seat path this is done: two players pair over a real shared link and both claim a port. Ports 3 and 4 are no longer counted here -- they are not a transport gap but an engine one (#40, out of goal), and the lobby now says so on the tile instead of promising a fix: an unreachable tile reads "2P only" (lobby.mjs:347) and the spec's P3/P4 are drawn unavailable to match. The link is a private tailnet address, shared privately rather than published, so the server needs no auth gate of its own. The two requests on this issue are split out so the board can pin them separately: #44 (the "copy link" text, comment 3076) and #45 (a list of open lobbies, comment 3101).

issues.title: Boot flags are bound to the room code, not to the URL
issues.pin: Owner ruling landed: a load mints a new room code. Implemented -- states.mjs withRoom mints a room onto the state search, with a test that fails if a stored room rides along. The strip happens earlier, in saveSearch, so no state this build writes carries a room at all; withRoom overrides the one a hand-edited or older store can still hold. Reason: a preset load is a reload (no snapshot path in the browser build), so the old room already saw this player leave and reassigned the port. Rejoining it would make the two sides disagree about the port map. Unblocks #22.

issues.title: Drop-in join
issues.pin: Taking a free port has to reach a match already running. Blocked, and not on the transport: the browser build defines no MELEE_STATE_SECTIONS, so snapshot_take() refuses every call and netplay is lockstep-only. See #34 and comment 2989 for the prerequisite order.

issues.title: Browser bypasses the lockstep guard
issues.pin: Why drop-in join is blocked: CMakeLists.txt:374 fails the build on a platform with no snapshot sections, and the browser target never reaches that check. Every online session silently degrades to lockstep.

issues.title: Spectators and the room roster
issues.pin: The owner ruled the port queue out: "there's no 'up next'. it's just a lobby that people can take ports on. like a living room with people and a gamecube, anyone can do whatever" (comment 3880). So the ordering is gone from all four layers -- the server keeps no queue and promotes nobody, a freed port is takeable by anyone, a taken one answers 409 and enrols the claimant in nothing, and the lobby draws no #queue line. What remains is the half the ruling keeps: #here lists who is in the room, read off the signalling server's subscriber map, which the close handler already prunes. The demo's old "2 watching" count is gone, since no message carried it and the list says more anyway. Measured over three real subscriptions: the server publishes here:[kiri,guest-4f,mango] and the lobby draws "In the room: kiri, guest-4f, mango". Past the seat count everybody simply watches: #no-port tells a portless visitor "Spectating - you hold no port - take a free one", and #31 marks the tile of whoever does hold one. The transport for more peers is #40 and out of goal.

issues.title: Export pc_net_connect so a net session can start (invalid)
issues.pin: INVALID -- the cause was wrong, and closing it rather than rewriting it so the board stops implying a one-line fix. pc_net_connect does not need an export: browser_net_start (platforms/browser/main.c:95) wraps it, is EMSCRIPTEN_KEEPALIVE and is already in -sEXPORTED_FUNCTIONS, and shell.mjs:442 already ccalls it. Two-player netplay runs through that path today, so nothing was blocked. The real limit on a third player is an engine design limit, now tracked as #40: net.c:2161 collapses the player argument to a boolean (net.local = player ? 1 : 0; net.remote = 1 - net.local), there is one remote input ring (net.c:65-68), and per-frame injection fills 2 of the 4 pad ports (net.c:2736,2745).

Two rules are written down with the measurement behind them: read source to source, and check a claim about the C against pc_stubs.c and the browser source list rather than launcher.cpp, which the browser never compiles. platforms/browser/README.md points at it from its Testing section.

issues.title: Gate demo-to-artifact parity; --audit does not cover it
issues.pin: Closed. The gate exists: build.py --parity walks mockup.TABS row tuples against settings.mjs, and --gate reports the count. Both sides are read statically, because a rendered DOM lists what exists and cannot show what is missing -- a subset of 12 rows looks like success until you set it beside the demo's 29. The spec side walks the tuples rather than grepping ctl-[a-z-]+ out of the file text, so an id that appears only in a comment or in prose cannot read as declared. The artifact side reads its tab list from the exported TABS array, not from the tabs its rows happen to use: a tab the artifact builds and leaves empty would otherwise be invisible, which is this issue's own blind spot one level down. Reported, not enforced: the 10 missing rows are tracked engine work (#3, #4, #32 and others), so a red gate would be permanent and would train everyone to ignore it. A broken extraction is a different matter and asserts, because a dead walk would report every artifact control as undeclared and look alarming while meaning nothing. Measured now: spec 29 rows over 5 tabs, artifact 19 over 4, 10 missing, 0 undeclared, Input absent. That is 11 mismatches and the number the board quotes each wave is no longer computed by hand.
issues.proof: /usr/bin/python3 tools/progress/build.py --parity-selftest >/dev/null && /usr/bin/python3 tools/progress/build.py --parity | grep -q 'parity: spec rows='

issues.title: Three and four player netplay needs an N-way engine net layer
issues.pin: OUT OF GOAL -- recorded so the board stops blaming a wasm export for it, not because it is queued. The standing goal is two people on two phones, which works. Seating a third is an engine rewrite, measured: the session holds one local and one remote and no player table (net_internal.h:349); net.c:2161 collapses the player argument to a boolean and derives remote = 1 - local, so seats 2 and 3 cannot be named; there is one remote input ring and one have/newest counter (net.c:65-68) that wait_remote waits on (net.c:1569); per-frame injection fills exactly 2 of the 4 pad ports (net.c:2736,2745); the handshake branches on local==0/1 (net_handshake.c:751, net_sync.c:182,251); net_rank.h:18-32 is fixed [2] arrays. There is no PC_NET_MAX_PLAYERS -- PC_LAN_MAX_PEERS 8 (net_lan.h:19) sizes LAN discovery, not seats. Lifting it needs per-seat tables and rings, a wait on the minimum across peers, and a peer-addressed transport. Only then do the browser caps matter, and they are the smaller half: signal.mjs claims are literally [null,null] with a 400 above slot 1 (:6,:65,:99), offer/answer are broadcast with no addressing so 3+ peers cannot pair, shell.mjs holds one RTCPeerConnection, net_rtc.c carries one channel with no peer id, and lobby.mjs:34 PAIRABLE=2 gates the UI.

issues.title: Two players on two real phones through one shared link
issues.pin: The standing goal, and the one pin whose closing needs a measurement no other pin makes. #6 measured two browsers pairing over a routable https origin, one of them phone-shaped -- a viewport, not a phone. This closes when two actual handsets open the same link, both claim a port, and a match runs with the touch overlay driving it on both. Until that is measured the board should not read as done, however green the gates are.

Closed: all five exist in settings.mjs LIVE (volume, music, sfx, reverb, aspect), 5 of 5. Each calls its exported C setter directly while the engine runs (pc_audio_set_volume, _music_volume, _sfx_volume, pc_audio_set_reverb, pc_widescreen_set_mode) and persists in localStorage as melee.live.<fn>. They are never in the URL: a slider behind a page reload would cost the player the match, and a value in the URL would carry your volume to a friend through a shared room link.

issues.title: Lobby: list open lobbies to join
issues.pin: Built. Join lists the open lobbies and a press goes to one. The three halves the last pin named as missing all landed: the signal server enumerates rooms (GET /rooms, signal.mjs:46, returning name/here/free per room), the button has a handler (lobby.mjs:267, the same onJoin shape as onLoad), and the list itself is platforms/browser/join.mjs, a <dialog> mirroring the save-state modal. free counts the two pairable slots the transport actually carries, not all four ports, so a tile cannot report a seat netplay would refuse. A full room is listed disabled and says "(full)" rather than vanishing, because a room that silently leaves the list reads as a fault. The modal shows itself on the press and fills afterwards: awaiting the fetch first left Join looking dead for as long as the signal server took, and an unreachable server is the normal case for a visitor who was sent a link, so that path renders a line and never throws out of open(). Seven tests in tests/browser/join.test.mjs, two of them against a real http server. What is NOT built: no room has a name a human chose, so the list shows the minted hex, and nothing filters or sorts it -- fine while a room lives only as long as a stream.
issues.proof: cd /home/kiri/wt-mp-parity && N=/home/kiri/.nvm/versions/node/v20.5.1/bin/node && $N --test --test-name-pattern 'the modal is shut until Join is pressed, and shuts again on Close' tests/browser/join.test.mjs 2>&1 | grep -qx '# pass 1' && $N --test --test-name-pattern 'pressing a room navigates to that room and to no other' tests/browser/join.test.mjs 2>&1 | grep -qx '# pass 1' && $N --test --test-name-pattern 'a room with no free seat is disabled and says so, a room with one is pressable' tests/browser/join.test.mjs 2>&1 | grep -qx '# pass 1' && $N --test --test-name-pattern 'the rooms endpoint reports occupancy and free seats' tests/browser/join.test.mjs 2>&1 | grep -qx '# pass 1' && $N --test --test-name-pattern 'the modal opens on the press, before the room list has arrived' tests/browser/join.test.mjs 2>&1 | grep -qx '# pass 1' && grep -q 'if (onJoin) join.addEventListener' platforms/browser/lobby.mjs

issues.title: Shared settings manifest so parity checks the loop at its source
issues.pin: The settings rows are built by a loop on both sides, so a grep over index.html scores all 27 as absent and --parity cannot check them. Measured against the mockup today: 23 of the 29 demo rows are built and render on the wire, and 0 are extra. The 6 that are not built are ctl-hud-mode, ctl-filter, ctl-custom-textures, ctl-mute, ctl-net-name and ctl-net-relay. None of them is UI work. Probed each against EXPORTED_FUNCTIONS in platforms/browser/CMakeLists.txt, with pc_audio_set_reverb as a supported-sibling control that scores 1: all 6 score 0, so no JavaScript can reach them. hud_mode and custom_textures are named in src/pc/pc.h but are still not exported; filter_mode, anisotropy, mute and net_name have no setter at all. #28 is closed and covers these rows, so nothing tracked the remaining 6 and the gap was re-derived each wave. This pin holds them until the manifest lands.
